A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Scaling with Collapse research and Celerity models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original training sweeps, Celerity model evaluations, collapse analyses, and early-stopping experiments in Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds validation-loss trajectories for four Celerity model sizes in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The architectures, CompleteP/AdamW training recipe, collapse normalization, and predictor in Equations 4–5 remain unchanged. Section 5's six-step procedure expands the explanation of the existing alignment and early-stopping approach.

E1.justification: The training corpora and seven downstream tasks are retained. The added validation analysis uses a held-out SlimPajama split for the existing language-modeling task. Consolidating the SlimPajama mixture rows does not establish changed data coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10 contain the same 61 model and compute-accounting rows, including Llama-3 and Qwen models already present in v1. The parameterization, early-stopping, and predictor-ablation comparators are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds evaluation at 5% training intervals on a fixed 493M-token SlimPajama holdout for four Celerity sizes trained to 80 TPP. V2 Table 4 also corrects the 3.3B/30-TPP token budget from 76.5B to 99.8B; this reported correction does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 and Figure 21 examine whether collapse extends to validation-loss trajectories. V1 mentioned held-out agreement but lacked this four-model, 80-TPP analysis. Existing schedule, momentum, MoE, dataset, and predictor analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added. Existing curve counts and correlation reporting remain unchanged, and Appendix A still identifies seed-bootstrap uncertainty as future work.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 21 newly shows closely aligned normalized validation losses across four Celerity sizes, apart from early checkpoints. All matched downstream scores, prediction MAEs, ablation values, and existing plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–24 and the derivations in Appendices B.2, B.3, and C.1 are retained. The new notation table and rewritten bias–variance explanation restate existing mathematics without changing assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about collapse controls, Celerity's efficiency, diagnostic monitoring, and hyperparameter selection after 10–30% of training. The added validation evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 discusses validation monitoring under curricula and preserving the timescale during batch-size scheduling. Appendix C.3 replaces the stated Llama-3 exclusion with a comparison qualified by token-budget assumptions. Its new blanket claim that these smaller models exceed 10^24 FLOPs conflicts with Table 10, including Llama-3.2-1B at 5.29×10^23.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies that displayed batch sizes use sequences, adds a CompleteP sample-code link, and documents validation checkpoints and sample size. Conversely, v1 Table 5's five SlimPajama subset percentages become one 17.49% entry in v2 Table 6, removing recipe detail while explicitly stating that C4 and CommonCrawl are excluded.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bottou et al. (2018) for optimization background and Meterez et al. (2025) for scheduling, and expands connections to Dey's parameterization results. The central positioning relative to Qiu's collapse work and scaling-law research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a conceptual Background introduction, expands the bias–variance explanation, and organizes the existing early-stopping procedure into six steps. These localized revisions, Appendix C.5, and wording refinements preserve the overall section order and most of the narrative.

P2.justification: The document receives a broad visual redesign with Cerebras branding, different typography, headers, footers, and figure placement. Wrapped displays become standalone floats; a notation table and validation figure are added, mixture rows are consolidated, and full evaluation and MAE tables move to the end. Existing result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The held-out validation analysis, clearer early-stopping explanation, corrected token budget, and explicit batch-size units modestly strengthen evidence and usability. These gains are tempered by lost SlimPajama mixture detail and the inaccurate blanket FLOPs statement in Appendix C.3. The central method and existing performance evidence remain stable.
